newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Sept existing home sales fell 2.9 pct - NAR.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Sept existing home sales fell 2.9 pct - NAR.

text.p: Sales of existing U.S. homes fell 2.9 percent in September to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 4.02 million units from a revised 4.14 million units in August, the National Association of Realtors said Friday.
The September sales rate was also down 1.7 percent from sales of 4.09 million in September last year.
August sales were revised to a 0.2 percent drop. The NAR previously said August sales fell 0.5 percent to 4.13 million units.
Wall Street economists had forecast September sales of 4.11 million units.

NAR President Art Godi said the September sales figures reflect consumer caution in the wake of higher interest rates.
But NAR Chief Economist John Tuccillo said mortgage rates have likely peaked for the year.
"We expect rates to begin to drift down through the rest of the year," Tuccillo said.
